title: 60 SQL Practice Queries with Answers: PostgreSQL Drills
summary: Sixty graded PostgreSQL 16 drills on one employees/departments/orders schema, ordered from basic SELECTs to real interview problems. Every task has runnable solution code and the exact result it returns on the sample data.

chapters.title: 60 SQL Queries on PostgreSQL
points: Engine: PostgreSQL 16, one shared schema of employees, departments and orders
Eight task families from basic to advanced
Basics and Filtering: SELECT, ORDER BY, LIMIT, WHERE, LIKE, NULL
Aggregates and Joins: GROUP BY, HAVING, inner, left and self joins
Subqueries and Window Functions: EXISTS, RANK, LAG, running totals
CTEs and Interview Scenarios: recursive CTEs, nth highest salary, duplicates

chapters.title: The Practice Schema and Sample Rows
points: departments(id, name, location): 4 rows such as Engineering/Austin, Sales/Denver, HR/Austin, Finance/Boston
employees(id, name, email, dept_id, manager_id, job_title, salary, hire_date): 10 sample rows
orders(id, employee_id, customer, amount, order_date, status): 12 sample rows
Relationships: employees.dept_id references departments.id, employees.manager_id references employees.id, orders.employee_id references employees.id
Deliberate edge cases in the data: a CEO with NULL manager_id, a department with no employees, an employee with no orders, a duplicated email
Conventions: PostgreSQL 16, lowercase snake_case, results shown exactly as psql returns them

chapters.title: Basics: SELECT, Sort and Limit
points: Task: List every column of every department with SELECT * FROM departments
Task: Show only name and salary of all employees
Task: Rename salary as annual_salary using a column alias
Task: Sort employees by salary from highest to lowest
Task: Return the three highest-paid employees with ORDER BY and LIMIT 3
Task: List each distinct job_title once with SELECT DISTINCT
Task: Build a label like 'Asha - Engineer' with the || concatenation operator
Task: Show each salary after a 10% raise rounded to 2 decimals with ROUND(salary * 1.10, 2)

chapters.title: Filtering: WHERE, LIKE, NULL and CASE
points: Task: Find employees earning between 50000 and 80000 with BETWEEN
Task: Find employees in departments 1 or 3 using IN
Task: Find employees whose name starts with 'A' using ILIKE for case-insensitive match
Task: Find the employee with no manager using IS NULL, not = NULL
Task: Find Engineering staff earning over 90000 or anyone titled Manager, with parentheses fixing AND/OR precedence
Task: Return orders whose status is not 'cancelled', and see why NULL status rows vanish
Task: Label each employee Junior, Mid or Senior by salary band with CASE WHEN
Task: Fetch rows 4 to 6 of the salary ranking with LIMIT and OFFSET

chapters.title: Aggregates: GROUP BY and HAVING
points: Task: Count all employees, and count only those with a manager using COUNT(*) versus COUNT(manager_id)
Task: Compute average salary per department with GROUP BY dept_id
Task: Sum order amount per employee
Task: List departments with more than 2 employees using HAVING COUNT(*) > 2
Task: Find the earliest and latest hire dates with MIN and MAX
Task: Count distinct customers who placed orders with COUNT(DISTINCT customer)
Task: Count shipped versus cancelled orders in a single row using FILTER (WHERE ...)
Task: List employee names per department as one comma-separated string with string_agg

chapters.title: Joins: Inner, Left, Self and Anti
points: Task: Show each employee with their department name using INNER JOIN
Task: List all departments including those with no employees using LEFT JOIN
Task: Show each employee next to their manager's name with a self join
Task: Find employees who earn more than their manager with a self join and a salary comparison
Task: Find employees with no orders using LEFT JOIN ... WHERE o.id IS NULL (anti-join)
Task: Total order amount per department name by joining three tables
Task: Use JOIN ... USING (id) shorthand where the key column names match
Task: Use FULL OUTER JOIN to list unmatched rows on both sides of departments and employees

chapters.title: Subqueries: Scalar, IN and EXISTS
points: Task: Find employees earning above the company average using a scalar subquery
Task: Find the employee with the maximum salary using WHERE salary = (SELECT MAX(salary) ...)
Task: Find employees working in departments located in Austin with IN (subquery)
Task: Find employees who have at least one order using EXISTS
Task: Find employees earning above their own department's average with a correlated subquery
Task: Find departments with no employees using NOT EXISTS, and why NOT IN breaks on NULLs
Task: Find the department with the highest total payroll using a subquery in FROM

chapters.title: Window Functions: Rank, Lag and Running Totals
points: Task: Number employees by salary with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC)
Task: Compare RANK and DENSE_RANK on tied salaries
Task: Find the top earner in each department with PARTITION BY and a rank filter
Task: Show each order next to the employee's previous order amount using LAG
Task: Show each order next to the next order date using LEAD
Task: Compute a running total of order amount by date with SUM() OVER (ORDER BY ...)
Task: Compute a 3-order moving average with ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
Task: Split employees into 4 salary quartiles with NTILE(4)

chapters.title: CTEs: WITH and Recursive Queries
points: Task: Rewrite a nested average-salary query as a readable WITH clause
Task: Chain two CTEs: department averages, then employees above their department average
Task: Walk the management chain from the CEO down with WITH RECURSIVE
Task: Add a depth column to the org chart so each level is numbered
Task: Generate the numbers 1 to 10 with a recursive CTE
Task: Compute month-over-month order growth with a CTE plus LAG

chapters.title: Interview Scenarios: Nth Highest, Duplicates, Running Totals
points: Task: Find the 3rd highest distinct salary with DENSE_RANK in a CTE
Task: Find the second highest salary with OFFSET 1, returning NULL when it does not exist
Task: Find the second highest salary in each department
Task: Find duplicate emails with GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
Task: Delete duplicate employee rows keeping the lowest id, using DELETE ... USING
Task: Build a monthly revenue report with a cumulative running total using date_trunc and SUM OVER
Task: Compute the median salary with percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP

chapters.title: SQL Cheatsheet: Pattern for Every Family
points: Clause order written: SELECT, FROM, JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT
Run order: FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY, LIMIT
WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after
NULL rules: use IS NULL, COUNT(col) skips NULLs, NOT IN fails on NULLs
Join picker: INNER for matches, LEFT plus IS NULL for anti-join, self join for hierarchies
Ranking picker: ROW_NUMBER unique, RANK leaves gaps, DENSE_RANK has none
nth highest recipe: DENSE_RANK in a CTE, then WHERE rnk = n
Recursive CTE shape: anchor UNION ALL recursive step, with a stop condition
